summary: North Fork Valley Airport (WPO) is a small general aviation airfield serving Paonia, Colorado, nestled in the scenic North Fork Valley of the Gunnison River on Colorado's Western Slope. The airport supports recreational flying, agricultural aviation, and serves the surrounding rural communities known for orchards, vineyards, and organic farming. Its location amid dramatic mountain terrain makes it a popular stopover for pilots exploring the Rocky Mountains.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft can use North Fork Valley Airport?
A: The airport primarily accommodates small general aviation aircraft and is not served by commercial airlines.

Q: Are there any scheduled flights at WPO?
A: No, North Fork Valley Airport does not offer scheduled commercial service. All flights are private or charter-based.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features a single runway and basic general aviation amenities; there is no large terminal or commercial infrastructure.

Q: Is the airport open to public use?
A: Yes, it is a public-use airport available to general aviation pilots, though prior permission or radio contact may be advisable.
transport_tips: Since the airport has no commercial service, visitors typically need a personal vehicle or rental car to reach Paonia from larger airports like Grand Junction Regional (GJT) or Montrose Regional (MTJ), each roughly 60–70 miles away. Local taxi and ride-share services are limited in this rural area, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended. The drive from the airport into Paonia is short, just a few minutes along local roads.
local_tip: Frequent visitors recommend flying in during late spring or early fall to enjoy the valley's orchards and vineyards at their peak, and to be prepared for afternoon mountain weather—thermal winds can pick up quickly and affect takeoff and landing conditions.
